what: Initial retry plan does not preserve BEHIND routing after UNKNOWN recovery
scenario_or_breakage: If the first gh response is UNKNOWN but a retry resolves to BEHIND, the proposed flow skips the existing early BEHIND exit and reaches CI first; pending CI would emit ci_not_ready instead of main_advanced, and passing CI would emit main_advanced with a misleading Branch mergeStateStatus error despite the plan saying BEHIND handling is out of scope
suggested_fix: After the initial retry/exhaustion check, re-check BEHIND before refresh_ci_state, or move the retry block before a single BEHIND gate; add a G case for UNKNOWN resolving to BEHIND with non-pass CI

what: Plan explicitly omits the sibling contract doc even though merge-pr.sh behavior changes
scenario_or_breakage: The shipped contract would still say empty/UNKNOWN short-circuits and that failure handling is unchanged, which becomes false after adding the initial 4-retry path; this also violates the sibling-doc rule requiring behavior changes and script docs to stay in sync
suggested_fix: Add scripts/merge-pr.md to the plan and update the error row plus Batched discovery prose to describe 4 retries with 5-second sleeps before failing, and transient resolution continuing through normal routing

what: [OUT_OF_SCOPE] Post-force-push UNKNOWN retry has the same missing BEHIND re-check
scenario_or_breakage: If post-force-push UNKNOWN resolves to BEHIND, CI can be checked before branch staleness is reported, so pending CI may mask main advancement
suggested_fix: Track a follow-up to re-check BEHIND immediately after post-force-push UNKNOWN recovery and cover it with a Q/R-adjacent harness case
